summary: Pope County, IL, steel lookout on the Shawnee National Forest; offered for sale with seven other towers in 1972; listed as gone.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: Southern Illinoisan notice inviting bids for the sale of this tower and seven other steel lookout towers on the Shawnee National Forest (August 18, 1972)

evidence.supports: newspaper that carried the August 18, 1972 advertisement for bids

evidence.supports: listed as gone in the FFLA Illinois list
Forest Service: Trigg is the only remaining of the 16 fire lookouts on the Shawnee National Forest
evidence.quote: Trigg Lookout Tower is the only remaining of the 16 fire lookouts constructed on the Shawnee National Forest.

evidence.supports: Frakes visited 17 Illinois sites; almost all towers taken down or sold in the early 1970s
evidence.quote: Of the towers in Illinois, he was able to visit 17 sites and climb four of them before almost all were taken down or sold in the early 1970s.

evidence.supports: Frakes is a historian of fire lookouts
evidence.quote: Since childhood, Frakes has been an avid fan and historian of anything having to do with fire lookouts.

notes_for_editor: Only the 1972 sale notice dates this tower; the Forest Lookouts page confirms the Southern Illinoisan date and calls the item an advertisement. No construction date, height, staffing or removal record was found in the sources read, so the story omits them. The Frakes statement about Illinois towers in general is context, not a McCormick-specific claim. The Forest Lookouts page gives no site description. The 1937 Melcher Hill report says three more secondary towers were planned, one at Benham Hill in Pope County; no source ties that to McCormick, so it is not used. A Facebook group thread on Pope County towers appeared in search results only and was not read. Access is left out: the sources place the site in the Shawnee National Forest but say nothing about what is there now.
